items.note: The page states the identity $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot\frac{a*(\overline a\cdot u)}{T}$ under the paper's hypothesis that every $t_i$ is even. It proves it the paper's way: periodicity of $a$, then expanding $(j_i-k_i)^2$ to match the coefficient of $u_{\boldsymbol k}$ against that of $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$, with $Q$ defined as reading frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$, which matches $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$.

This is a definition, and the page gives it exactly: "Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$ and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate". This matches paper line 3916.

The page computes $-\pi i s_i\frac{(j_i+t_i)^2-j_i^2}{t_i}=-\pi i s_i(2j_i+t_i)$ and says it is a multiple of $2\pi i$ "because $t_i$ is even", which gives period $t_i$. It also explains why periodicity is needed (the convolution reads $a$ modulo $t_i$). This is the paper's argument, with the even-$t_i$ hypothesis spelled out.

The page writes the coefficient as $\frac1T\overline a_{\boldsymbol j}a_{\boldsymbol j-\boldsymbol k}\overline a_{\boldsymbol k}$ and expands $(j_i-k_i)^2=j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2$. The exponent $\sum_i\frac{\pi i s_i}{t_i}(j_i^2-(j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2)+k_i^2)$ is correct and reduces to $2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i$, as in the paper. A $d=1$, $t_1=2$ example checks it correctly.

The page defines $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ with the negative sign and normalization $1/T$, and defines $Q$ as putting frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$ at position $\boldsymbol j$. It gives the resulting coefficient $\frac1T\exp(2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i)$ and concludes that it matches "because $Q$ reads frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$ from the negative-sign transform". The substitution $f_i=-s_ij_i$ is left implicit, as in the paper, but every ingredient is on the page.

errors.quote: Executing $Q$ means sorting data on tapes, which costs a logarithmic factor beyond a linear pass, the kind of factor the power saving removes.
errors.problem: The power saving removes a factor $(\lg n)^{\kappa}$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, a tiny fractional power of the logarithm, not a full logarithmic factor. In the paper, the label-and-sort implementation of $P_t$ costs $O(tp\log t)$ (line 3693). That full log factor would wipe out the saving; it is not the same kind of factor the saving removes.
